t: Users, groups and RBAC
Users, groups aur RBAC
goal: Give a group Reader on one resource group and prove what its member can do.
Ek group ko ek resource group par Reader dein aur dekhein us ka member kya kar sakta hai.
skills: Create users and groups
Manage user and group properties
Manage built-in Azure roles
Assign roles at different scopes
Interpret access assignments

t: Create a resource group and read your tenant's default domain.
Resource group banayen aur tenant ka default domain lein.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab01
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
DOMAIN=$(az rest --method get --url https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/domains --query "value[?isDefault].id" -o tsv)
echo $DOMAIN

t: Create a user with a random password (you don't need to sign in as them).
Random password wala user banayen (us se sign in karna zaroori nahi).
steps.cli:
az ad user create --display-name "Lab User" --user-principal-name labuser1@$DOMAIN --password "$(openssl rand -base64 18)Aa1!" --force-change-password-next-sign-in true
USER_ID=$(az ad user show --id labuser1@$DOMAIN --query id -o tsv)

t: Create a security group and add the user.
Security group banayen aur user ko us mein dalein.
steps.cli:
az ad group create --display-name lab-readers --mail-nickname lab-readers
GROUP_ID=$(az ad group show --group lab-readers --query id -o tsv)
az ad group member add --group lab-readers --member-id $USER_ID

t: Assign Reader to the group on the resource group only.
Group ko sirf resource group par Reader dein.
steps.cli:
SCOPE=$(az group show -n $RG --query id -o tsv)
az role assignment create --assignee-object-id $GROUP_ID --assignee-principal-type Group --role Reader --scope $SCOPE

t: In the portal: resource group → Access control (IAM) → Check access → Lab User. Reader shows up through the group.
Portal mein: resource group → Access control (IAM) → Check access → Lab User. Reader group ke zariye dikhega.
In the portal: Microsoft Entra ID → Users → Lab User. Set the department and usage location under Properties.
Portal mein: Microsoft Entra ID → Users → Lab User. Properties mein department aur usage location set karein.

remember: Permissions come from the group: remove the member and the access is gone.
Permission group se aati hai: member nikalein to access khatam.
Assigning roles needs Owner or User Access Administrator, not Contributor.
Role dene ke liye Owner ya User Access Administrator chahiye, Contributor nahi.
cleanup:
az group delete -n $RG --yes --no-wait
az ad group delete --group lab-readers
az ad user delete --id labuser1@$DOMAIN

t: Policy, tags and locks
Policy, tags aur locks
goal: See a Deny policy block a deployment and a lock block a deletion.
Deny policy ko deployment aur lock ko delete rokte hue dekhein.
skills: Implement and manage Azure Policy
Configure resource locks
Apply and manage tags on resources
Manage resource groups

t: Create a resource group with a tag.
Tag wala resource group banayen.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab02
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope --tags env=lab
SCOPE=$(az group show -n $RG --query id -o tsv)

t: Assign the built-in policy that requires a tag on resources.
Built-in policy assign karein jo resources par tag lazmi karti hai.
steps.cli:
POLICY=$(az policy definition list --query "[?displayName=='Require a tag on resources'].name" -o tsv)
az policy assignment create --name require-env --scope $SCOPE --policy $POLICY --params '{"tagName":{"value":"env"}}'

t: Wait 5 to 15 minutes, then try to create an untagged storage account. It must fail with RequestDisallowedByPolicy.
5 se 15 minute rukein, phir baghair tag storage account banayen. RequestDisallowedByPolicy ke sath fail hona chahiye.
steps.cli:
SA=az104lab$RANDOM$RANDOM
az storage account create -n $SA -g $RG --sku Standard_LRS

t: Try again with the tag. It works.
Tag ke sath dobara koshish karein. Ban jayega.
steps.cli: az storage account create -n $SA -g $RG --sku Standard_LRS --tags env=lab

t: Add a second tag without losing the first.
Pehla tag khoye baghair doosra tag lagayen.
steps.cli:
ID=$(az storage account show -n $SA -g $RG --query id -o tsv)
az tag update --resource-id $ID --operation Merge --tags costcenter=100

t: Lock the group and try to delete the account. It must fail with ScopeLocked.
Group par lock lagayen aur account delete karein. ScopeLocked ke sath fail hona chahiye.
steps.cli:
az lock create --name keep --lock-type CanNotDelete --resource-group $RG
az storage account delete -n $SA -g $RG --yes

t: In the portal: Policy → Compliance. Open the assignment and see what is evaluated.
Portal mein: Policy → Compliance. Assignment khol kar dekhein kya evaluate hua.

remember: Policy stops even an Owner. A lock does too.
Policy Owner ko bhi rokti hai. Lock bhi.
The account didn't get the group's tag: tags aren't inherited.
Account ko group ka tag nahi mila: tags inherit nahi hote.
cleanup:
az lock delete --name keep --resource-group $RG
az policy assignment delete --name require-env --scope $SCOPE
az group delete -n $RG --yes --no-wait

t: Blob storage: SAS, versions and lifecycle
Blob storage: SAS, versions aur lifecycle
goal: Share one blob without an account key, recover an overwritten blob, and tier old data.
Account key ke baghair ek blob share karein, overwrite hua blob wapas layen, aur purana data tier karein.
skills: Create and configure storage accounts
Create and configure a container in Azure Blob Storage
Create and use shared access signature (SAS) tokens
Configure soft delete for blobs and containers
Configure blob versioning
Configure blob lifecycle management
Configure storage tiers

t: Create the account and give yourself a blob data role (Owner alone can't read blobs).
Account banayen aur khud ko blob data role dein (sirf Owner blobs nahi parh sakta).
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab03
SA=az104lab$RANDOM$RANDOM
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az storage account create -n $SA -g $RG --sku Standard_LRS --kind StorageV2 --allow-blob-public-access false
SA_ID=$(az storage account show -n $SA -g $RG --query id -o tsv)
az role assignment create --assignee $(az ad signed-in-user show --query id -o tsv) --role "Storage Blob Data Contributor" --scope $SA_ID

t: Turn on versioning and 7-day soft delete.
Versioning aur 7 din ka soft delete on karein.
steps.cli: az storage account blob-service-properties update -n $SA -g $RG --enable-versioning true --enable-delete-retention true --delete-retention-days 7

t: Create a container and upload a file (wait a few minutes if the role isn't active yet).
Container banayen aur file upload karein (role abhi active na ho to chand minute rukein).
steps.cli:
echo "version 1" > note.txt
az storage container create --account-name $SA -n docs --auth-mode login
az storage blob upload --account-name $SA -c docs -f note.txt -n note.txt --auth-mode login

t: Make a user delegation SAS for one hour and read the blob with it.
Ek ghante ka user delegation SAS banayen aur us se blob parhein.
steps.cli:
END=$(date -u -d "1 hour" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%MZ')
URL=$(az storage blob generate-sas --account-name $SA -c docs -n note.txt --permissions r --expiry $END --as-user --auth-mode login --https-only --full-uri -o tsv)
curl "$URL"

t: Overwrite the blob. In the portal open the blob → Versions, choose the old one and Make current version.
Blob overwrite karein. Portal mein blob → Versions, purana chunein aur Make current version.
steps.cli:
echo "version 2" > note.txt
az storage blob upload --account-name $SA -c docs -f note.txt -n note.txt --overwrite --auth-mode login

t: Add a lifecycle rule: cool after 30 days, delete after 365.
Lifecycle rule lagayen: 30 din baad cool, 365 baad delete.
steps.cli:
cat > policy.json <<'EOF'
{"rules":[{"enabled":true,"name":"age","type":"Lifecycle","definition":{"filters":{"blobTypes":["blockBlob"]},"actions":{"baseBlob":{"tierToCool":{"daysAfterModificationGreaterThan":30},"delete":{"daysAfterModificationGreaterThan":365}}}}}]}
EOF
az storage account management-policy create --account-name $SA -g $RG --policy @policy.json

t: Change the blob's tier to Cool by hand and check it.
Blob ki tier haath se Cool karein aur dekhein.
steps.cli:
az storage blob set-tier --account-name $SA -c docs -n note.txt --tier Cool --auth-mode login
az storage blob show --account-name $SA -c docs -n note.txt --auth-mode login --query properties.blobTier

remember: --as-user needs --auth-mode login and an expiry: the SAS is signed with Entra ID, not a key.
--as-user ko --auth-mode login aur expiry chahiye: SAS Entra ID se signed hai, key se nahi.
Try curl again after an hour: the SAS no longer works.
Ek ghante baad curl dobara chalayen: SAS kaam nahi karega.

t: Azure Files: snapshot and soft delete
Azure Files: snapshot aur soft delete
goal: Recover one file from a snapshot and a whole share from soft delete.
Snapshot se ek file aur soft delete se poora share wapas layen.
skills: Create and configure a file share in Azure Files
Configure snapshots and soft delete for Azure Files
Manage access keys

t: Create the account and share, and turn on share soft delete.
Account aur share banayen, aur share soft delete on karein.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab04
SA=az104lab$RANDOM$RANDOM
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az storage account create -n $SA -g $RG --sku Standard_LRS --kind StorageV2
az storage account file-service-properties update -n $SA -g $RG --enable-delete-retention true --delete-retention-days 7
az storage share-rm create --storage-account $SA -g $RG -n docs --quota 10

t: Upload a file with the account key.
Account key se file upload karein.
steps.cli:
KEY=$(az storage account keys list -n $SA -g $RG --query "[0].value" -o tsv)
echo "important" > plan.txt
az storage file upload --account-name $SA --account-key $KEY --share-name docs --source plan.txt

t: Take a share snapshot, then delete the file.
Share snapshot lein, phir file delete karein.
steps.cli:
az storage share-rm snapshot --storage-account $SA -g $RG -n docs
az storage file delete --account-name $SA --account-key $KEY --share-name docs --path plan.txt

t: In the portal: share → Snapshots → open the snapshot → plan.txt → Restore. The file is back.
Portal mein: share → Snapshots → snapshot kholein → plan.txt → Restore. File wapas aa gayi.
Delete the whole share with its snapshots, and find it among deleted shares.
Snapshots samet poora share delete karein, aur deleted shares mein dhoondein.
steps.cli:
az storage share-rm delete --storage-account $SA -g $RG -n docs --include snapshots --yes
VER=$(az storage share-rm list --storage-account $SA -g $RG --include-deleted --query "[?name=='docs' && deleted].version | [0]" -o tsv)
echo $VER

t: Wait a minute, then restore the share.
Ek minute rukein, phir share wapas layen.
steps.cli: az storage share-rm restore --storage-account $SA -g $RG -n docs --deleted-version $VER

t: Rotate the key. The old value in $KEY stops working.
Key rotate karein. $KEY ki purani value kaam karna chhor deti hai.
steps.cli:
az storage account keys renew --account-name $SA -g $RG --key primary
az storage file list --account-name $SA --account-key $KEY --share-name docs

remember: Soft delete restores shares. Snapshots restore files.
Soft delete shares wapas lata hai. Snapshots files.
Rotating a key breaks everything that uses it, including SAS tokens signed with it.
Key rotate karne se us ka har istemal tootta hai, us se signed SAS bhi.

t: Bicep: what-if and deployment modes
Bicep: what-if aur deployment modes
goal: Preview and deploy a Bicep file, then see what Complete mode deletes.
Bicep file ka preview aur deploy karein, phir dekhein Complete mode kya delete karta hai.
skills: Interpret an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
Modify an existing Bicep file
Deploy resources by using an Azure Resource Manager template or a Bicep file
Export a deployment as an Azure Resource Manager template or convert an Azure Resource Manager template to a Bicep file

t: Create an empty resource group and write the Bicep file.
Khaali resource group banayen aur Bicep file likhein.
Preview, then deploy.
Preview karein, phir deploy.
steps.cli:
az deployment group what-if -g $RG --template-file main.bicep
az deployment group create -g $RG --template-file main.bicep --query properties.outputs.name.value

t: Try a value that isn't allowed. It must fail before anything is deployed.
Aisi value dein jo allowed nahi. Deploy se pehle fail hona chahiye.
steps.cli: az deployment group create -g $RG --template-file main.bicep --parameters sku=Premium_LRS

t: Create a public IP by hand, outside the template, and deploy again. Incremental mode keeps it.
Template ke bahar haath se public IP banayen aur dobara deploy karein. Incremental mode usay rakhta hai.
steps.cli:
az network public-ip create -g $RG -n extra --sku Standard
az deployment group create -g $RG --template-file main.bicep
az resource list -g $RG -o table

t: Preview Complete mode. What-if shows that the public IP would be deleted.
Complete mode ka preview karein. What-if dikhata hai ke public IP delete hoga.
steps.cli: az deployment group what-if -g $RG --template-file main.bicep --mode Complete

t: Run Complete mode (only in this lab group!) and list the resources.
Complete mode chalayen (sirf is lab group mein!) aur resources dekhein.
steps.cli:
az deployment group create -g $RG --template-file main.bicep --mode Complete
az resource list -g $RG -o table

t: Export the group to ARM JSON, then decompile it to Bicep and read the result.
Group ko ARM JSON mein export karein, phir Bicep mein decompile kar ke nateeja parhein.
steps.cli:
az group export -n $RG > exported.json
az bicep decompile --file exported.json --force
cat exported.bicep

remember: Complete mode deletes what the template doesn't contain. Never try it in a group you need.
Complete mode template mein na hone wala delete karta hai. Zaroori group mein kabhi na chalayen.
Decompiled Bicep needs a review: it's a best-effort conversion.
Decompile hui Bicep dekhni parti hai: koshish ki had tak conversion hai.

t: Virtual machine: disk, resize, deallocate
Virtual machine: disk, resize, deallocate
goal: Add a disk, resize the VM and see the difference between stopped and deallocated.
Disk lagayen, VM resize karein, aur stopped aur deallocated ka farq dekhein.
skills: Create a virtual machine
Manage virtual machine disks
Manage virtual machine sizes

t: Create a small Linux VM without any inbound port. If the size isn't available, choose another region or size.
Choti Linux VM banayen, koi inbound port nahi. Size na mile to doosra region ya size chunein.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab06
SIZE=Standard_B2ats_v2
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az vm create -g $RG -n vm1 --image Ubuntu2204 --size $SIZE --generate-ssh-keys --nsg-rule NONE

t: Run a command inside the VM without SSH.
SSH ke baghair VM ke andar command chalayen.
steps.cli: az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "lsblk" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

t: Attach a 32 GB data disk and look again.
32 GB data disk lagayen aur dobara dekhein.
steps.cli:
az vm disk attach -g $RG --vm-name vm1 --name data1 --new --size-gb 32 --sku Standard_LRS
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "lsblk" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

t: Stop the VM, check its state, then deallocate it and check again.
VM stop karein, state dekhein, phir deallocate karein aur dobara dekhein.
steps.cli:
az vm stop -g $RG -n vm1
az vm get-instance-view -g $RG -n vm1 --query "instanceView.statuses[1].displayStatus"
az vm deallocate -g $RG -n vm1
az vm get-instance-view -g $RG -n vm1 --query "instanceView.statuses[1].displayStatus"

t: See the sizes you can resize to, resize to a similar small one, and start the VM.
Resize ke sizes dekhein, kisi chote size par resize karein, aur VM start karein.
steps.cli:
az vm list-vm-resize-options -g $RG -n vm1 --query "[?numberOfCores==\`2\`].name" -o tsv | head -20
az vm resize -g $RG -n vm1 --size Standard_B2als_v2
az vm start -g $RG -n vm1

t: In the portal: VM → Overview. Find the size, the disks and the auto-shutdown setting.
Portal mein: VM → Overview. Size, disks aur auto-shutdown setting dhoondein.

remember: 'VM stopped' is still billed for compute. 'VM deallocated' isn't (disks still cost).
'VM stopped' ka compute bill aata hai. 'VM deallocated' ka nahi (disks ka phir bhi).
Run Command needs outbound 443 from the VM to return its output.
Run Command ko output dene ke liye VM se outbound 443 chahiye.

t: Scale set with autoscale
Autoscale wala scale set
goal: Create a scale set and let CPU rules change the number of instances.
Scale set banayen aur CPU rules se instances ki tadaad badalne dein.
skills: Deploy and configure an Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets

t: Create a scale set with one instance.
Ek instance wala scale set banayen.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab07
SIZE=Standard_B2ats_v2
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az vmss create -g $RG -n vmss1 --image Ubuntu2204 --vm-sku $SIZE --instance-count 1 --orchestration-mode Flexible --generate-ssh-keys

t: Create autoscale settings: between 1 and 2 instances.
Autoscale settings banayen: 1 se 2 instances.
steps.cli: az monitor autoscale create -g $RG --resource vmss1 --resource-type Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachineScaleSets --name scale1 --min-count 1 --max-count 2 --count 1

t: Add a scale-out and a scale-in rule with a wide gap between them.
Scale-out aur scale-in rule lagayen, dono mein kaafi farq ke sath.
steps.cli:
az monitor autoscale rule create -g $RG --autoscale-name scale1 --condition "Percentage CPU > 70 avg 5m" --scale out 1
az monitor autoscale rule create -g $RG --autoscale-name scale1 --condition "Percentage CPU < 25 avg 5m" --scale in 1

t: Scale by hand and list the instances.
Haath se scale karein aur instances dekhein.
steps.cli:
az vmss scale -g $RG -n vmss1 --new-capacity 2
az vm list -g $RG -o table

t: In the portal: scale set → Scaling → Run history. After some idle minutes, autoscale goes back to 1.
Portal mein: scale set → Scaling → Run history. Kuch khaali minute baad autoscale wapas 1 par aata hai.

remember: Autoscale never leaves its minimum and maximum.
Autoscale minimum aur maximum se bahar nahi jata.
A small gap between the rules makes the instances flap.
Rules mein kam farq ho to instances bar bar ghat-ti barhti hain.

t: App Service slots and swap
App Service slots aur swap
goal: Swap a staging slot into production and see which setting stays with its slot.
Staging slot ko production mein swap karein aur dekhein kaun si setting slot ke sath rehti hai.
skills: Provision an App Service plan
Configure scaling for an App Service plan
Create an App Service
Configure deployment slots for an App Service

t: Create a Standard plan (slots need Standard or higher) and a web app.
Standard plan (slots ko Standard ya upar chahiye) aur web app banayen.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab08
APP=az104lab$RANDOM$RANDOM
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az appservice plan create -g $RG -n plan1 --sku S1 --is-linux
az webapp list-runtimes --os-type linux -o tsv | grep -i node
az webapp create -g $RG -p plan1 -n $APP --runtime "NODE:22-lts"

t: Create a staging slot.
Staging slot banayen.
steps.cli: az webapp deployment slot create -g $RG -n $APP --slot staging

t: Set a normal setting and a slot setting in both places.
Dono jagah ek aam setting aur ek slot setting lagayen.
steps.cli:
az webapp config appsettings set -g $RG -n $APP --settings VERSION=1 --slot-settings PLACE=production
az webapp config appsettings set -g $RG -n $APP --slot staging --settings VERSION=2 --slot-settings PLACE=staging

t: Swap and compare the settings. VERSION moved, PLACE stayed.
Swap karein aur settings ka muqabla karein. VERSION chali gayi, PLACE wahin rahi.
steps.cli:
az webapp deployment slot swap -g $RG -n $APP --slot staging --target-slot production
az webapp config appsettings list -g $RG -n $APP --query "[?name=='VERSION' || name=='PLACE'].{name:name,value:value}" -o table
az webapp config appsettings list -g $RG -n $APP --slot staging --query "[?name=='VERSION' || name=='PLACE'].{name:name,value:value}" -o table

t: Swap again: that's the rollback.
Dobara swap karein: yehi rollback hai.
steps.cli: az webapp deployment slot swap -g $RG -n $APP --slot staging --target-slot production

t: Scale the plan out to 2 instances, then try to scale it down to Basic. It must fail while the slot exists.
Plan ko 2 instances par scale out karein, phir Basic par lane ki koshish karein. Slot hote hue fail hona chahiye.
steps.cli:
az appservice plan update -g $RG -n plan1 --number-of-workers 2
az appservice plan update -g $RG -n plan1 --sku B1

remember: Slot settings don't swap. Use them for things that belong to the environment, such as a test database.
Slot settings swap nahi hoti. Environment ki cheezon ke liye, jaise test database.
Scale up = tier. Scale out = instances.
Scale up = tier. Scale out = instances.

t: Container Instances and Container Apps
Container Instances aur Container Apps
goal: Run one container in both services and compare them.
Ek container dono services mein chala kar muqabla karein.
skills: Provision a container by using Azure Container Instances
Provision a container by using Azure Container Apps
Manage sizing and scaling for containers, including Azure Container Instances and Azure Container Apps

t: Create a container instance with a public DNS name and open its address.
Public DNS naam wala container instance banayen aur address kholein.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab09
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.ContainerInstance
az container create -g $RG -n aci1 --image mcr.microsoft.com/azuredocs/aci-helloworld --os-type Linux --cpu 1 --memory 1.5 --ports 80 --ip-address Public --dns-name-label az104lab$RANDOM$RANDOM --query ipAddress.fqdn -o tsv

t: Read its logs, then look at its CPU and memory: they can't be changed in place.
Logs parhein, phir CPU aur memory dekhein: yeh chalte hue nahi badalte.
steps.cli:
az container logs -g $RG -n aci1
az container show -g $RG -n aci1 --query "containers[0].resources.requests"

t: Prepare Container Apps and create an environment.
Container Apps tayyar karein aur environment banayen.
steps.cli:
az extension add --name containerapp --upgrade
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.App
az provider register --namespace Microsoft.OperationalInsights
az containerapp env create -n env1 -g $RG -l westeurope --logs-destination none

t: Create an app that scales from 0 to 3 and open its address.
0 se 3 tak scale hone wali app banayen aur address kholein.
steps.cli: az containerapp create -n app1 -g $RG --environment env1 --image mcr.microsoft.com/k8se/quickstart:latest --target-port 80 --ingress external --min-replicas 0 --max-replicas 3 --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn -o tsv

t: Change the maximum. A new revision appears.
Maximum badlein. Naya revision ban jata hai.
steps.cli:
az containerapp update -n app1 -g $RG --max-replicas 5
az containerapp revision list -n app1 -g $RG -o table

t: Leave the app alone for some minutes, then list the replicas: it has scaled to zero.
App ko kuch minute chhor dein, phir replicas dekhein: zero tak scale ho chuki.
steps.cli: az containerapp replica list -n app1 -g $RG -o table

remember: ACI has no autoscale. Container Apps scale to zero.
ACI mein autoscale nahi. Container Apps zero tak scale hoti hain.
Changing the scale settings of a container app creates a new revision.
Container app ki scale settings badalne se naya revision banta hai.

t: Peering, routes and Next hop
Peering, routes aur Next hop
goal: Connect two VNets, then break the path with a route and find it with Network Watcher.
Do VNets jorein, phir route se raasta torein aur Network Watcher se dhoondein.
skills: Create and configure virtual networks and subnets
Create and configure virtual network peering
Configure user-defined routes
Troubleshoot network connectivity
Use Azure Network Watcher and Connection monitor

t: Create two VNets and a VM in each.
Do VNets aur har ek mein ek VM banayen.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab10
SIZE=Standard_B2ats_v2
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az network vnet create -g $RG -n vnet1 --address-prefix 10.1.0.0/16 --subnet-name s1 --subnet-prefix 10.1.1.0/24
az network vnet create -g $RG -n vnet2 --address-prefix 10.2.0.0/16 --subnet-name s2 --subnet-prefix 10.2.1.0/24
az vm create -g $RG -n vm1 --image Ubuntu2204 --size $SIZE --vnet-name vnet1 --subnet s1 --generate-ssh-keys --nsg-rule NONE
az vm create -g $RG -n vm2 --image Ubuntu2204 --size $SIZE --vnet-name vnet2 --subnet s2 --generate-ssh-keys --nsg-rule NONE

t: Test port 22 from vm1 to vm2 (10.2.1.4). It must be closed: the VNets aren't connected.
vm1 se vm2 (10.2.1.4) par port 22 test karein. Closed hona chahiye: VNets jure nahi.
steps.cli:
TEST="timeout 5 bash -c '</dev/tcp/10.2.1.4/22' && echo open || echo closed"
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "$TEST" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

t: Create one side of the peering and look at its state: Initiated.
Peering ki ek taraf banayen aur state dekhein: Initiated.
steps.cli:
az network vnet peering create -g $RG -n v1-to-v2 --vnet-name vnet1 --remote-vnet vnet2 --allow-vnet-access
az network vnet peering show -g $RG --vnet-name vnet1 -n v1-to-v2 --query peeringState

t: Create the other side and test again. Now it's open.
Doosri taraf banayen aur dobara test karein. Ab open hai.
steps.cli:
az network vnet peering create -g $RG -n v2-to-v1 --vnet-name vnet2 --remote-vnet vnet1 --allow-vnet-access
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "$TEST" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

t: Add a route that drops traffic to vnet2, and test again: closed.
Aisa route lagayen jo vnet2 ka traffic drop kare, aur test karein: closed.
steps.cli:
az network route-table create -g $RG -n rt1
az network route-table route create -g $RG --route-table-name rt1 -n drop --address-prefix 10.2.0.0/16 --next-hop-type None
az network vnet subnet update -g $RG --vnet-name vnet1 -n s1 --route-table rt1
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "$TEST" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

t: Find the cause: next hop and effective routes.
Wajah dhoondein: next hop aur effective routes.
steps.cli:
az network watcher show-next-hop -g $RG --vm vm1 --source-ip 10.1.1.4 --dest-ip 10.2.1.4
az network nic show-effective-route-table -g $RG -n vm1VMNic -o table

t: Remove the route table from the subnet and test once more.
Subnet se route table hatayen aur ek dafa phir test karein.
steps.cli:
az network vnet subnet update -g $RG --vnet-name vnet1 -n s1 --remove routeTable
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "$TEST" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

remember: Peering needs both sides. A UDR with the same prefix beats the peering route.
Peering ko dono taraf chahiye. Same prefix ki UDR peering route par bhari hai.
A route table works only when it's associated with a subnet.
Route table subnet se associate ho tabhi kaam karta hai.

t: NSG, ASG and IP flow verify
NSG, ASG aur IP flow verify
goal: Allow only web VMs to reach the database VM, and prove it without opening a session.
Sirf web VMs ko database VM tak jane dein, aur session khole baghair sabit karein.
skills: Create and configure network security groups (NSGs) and application security groups
Evaluate effective security rules in NSGs
Implement Azure Bastion

t: Create the network, an NSG on the subnet and two application security groups.
Network, subnet par NSG aur do application security groups banayen.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab11
SIZE=Standard_B2ats_v2
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az network nsg create -g $RG -n nsg1
az network vnet create -g $RG -n vnet1 --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16 --subnet-name app --subnet-prefix 10.0.1.0/24 --network-security-group nsg1
az network asg create -g $RG -n asg-web
az network asg create -g $RG -n asg-db

t: Create a web VM and a database VM without NSGs on their NICs.
NIC par NSG ke baghair web VM aur database VM banayen.
steps.cli:
az vm create -g $RG -n web1 --image Ubuntu2204 --size $SIZE --vnet-name vnet1 --subnet app --asgs asg-web --nsg "" --generate-ssh-keys
az vm create -g $RG -n db1 --image Ubuntu2204 --size $SIZE --vnet-name vnet1 --subnet app --asgs asg-db --nsg "" --generate-ssh-keys
WEB=$(az vm show -d -g $RG -n web1 --query privateIps -o tsv)
DB=$(az vm show -d -g $RG -n db1 --query privateIps -o tsv)
echo $WEB $DB

t: Add two rules: allow 1433 from asg-web to asg-db, and deny 1433 from everything else in the VNet.
Do rules lagayen: asg-web se asg-db tak 1433 allow, aur VNet ke baqi sab se 1433 deny.
steps.cli:
az network nsg rule create -g $RG --nsg-name nsg1 -n AllowWebToDb --priority 200 --direction Inbound --access Allow --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 1433 --source-asgs asg-web --destination-asgs asg-db
az network nsg rule create -g $RG --nsg-name nsg1 -n DenyOthersToDb --priority 300 --direction Inbound --access Deny --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 1433 --source-address-prefixes VirtualNetwork --destination-asgs asg-db

t: Ask IP flow verify: from the web VM it's allowed, from another address it's denied.
IP flow verify se poochein: web VM se allowed, doosre address se denied.
steps.cli:
az network watcher test-ip-flow -g $RG --vm db1 --direction Inbound --protocol TCP --local $DB:1433 --remote $WEB:50000
az network watcher test-ip-flow -g $RG --vm db1 --direction Inbound --protocol TCP --local $DB:1433 --remote 10.0.1.99:50000

t: Read the effective security rules of the database NIC.
Database NIC ke effective security rules parhein.
steps.cli: az network nic list-effective-nsg -g $RG -n db1VMNic

t: Optional, in the portal: VM web1 → Connect → Bastion. Bastion Developer is free where the region supports it. Dedicated Bastion is billed by the hour: don't deploy it for this lab. Port 22 is open inside the VNet by the default rule.

Optional, portal mein: VM web1 → Connect → Bastion. Bastion Developer free hai jahan region support kare. Dedicated Bastion ka bill per hour hai: is lab ke liye deploy na karein. VNet ke andar port 22 default rule se khula hai.

remember: The lowest number wins: swap the priorities and the web VM is blocked.
Sab se chota number jeetta hai: priorities badlein to web VM bhi block.
ASGs replace IP addresses: a new web VM only needs its NIC in the group.
ASG IP ki jagah leta hai: nayi web VM ka NIC bas group mein dalein.

t: Private endpoint and private DNS
Private endpoint aur private DNS
goal: Reach a storage account on a private IP and close its public access.
Storage account tak private IP par pahunchein aur us ka public access band karein.
skills: Configure private endpoints for Azure PaaS
Configure Azure DNS
Configure Azure Storage firewalls and virtual networks

t: Create a VNet, a VM and a storage account.
VNet, VM aur storage account banayen.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab12
SIZE=Standard_B2ats_v2
SA=az104lab$RANDOM$RANDOM
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az network vnet create -g $RG -n vnet1 --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16 --subnet-name app --subnet-prefix 10.0.1.0/24
az network vnet subnet create -g $RG --vnet-name vnet1 -n pe --address-prefixes 10.0.2.0/24
az vm create -g $RG -n vm1 --image Ubuntu2204 --size $SIZE --vnet-name vnet1 --subnet app --generate-ssh-keys --nsg-rule NONE
az storage account create -n $SA -g $RG --sku Standard_LRS --kind StorageV2

t: See what the name resolves to on the VM now: a public address.
Dekhein VM par naam abhi kis par resolve hota hai: public address.
steps.cli:
ASK="getent hosts $SA.blob.core.windows.net"
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "$ASK" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

t: Create the private endpoint for blob.
Blob ka private endpoint banayen.
steps.cli:
SA_ID=$(az storage account show -n $SA -g $RG --query id -o tsv)
az network private-endpoint create -g $RG -n pe1 --connection-name c1 --private-connection-resource-id $SA_ID --group-id blob --vnet-name vnet1 --subnet pe

t: Ask again: still public, because the DNS zone is missing.
Dobara poochein: abhi bhi public, kyunke DNS zone nahi.
steps.cli: az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "$ASK" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

t: Create the private DNS zone, link it to the VNet and connect it to the endpoint.
Private DNS zone banayen, VNet se link karein aur endpoint se jorein.
steps.cli:
ZONE=privatelink.blob.core.windows.net
az network private-dns zone create -g $RG -n $ZONE
az network private-dns link vnet create -g $RG --zone-name $ZONE -n link1 --virtual-network vnet1 --registration-enabled false
az network private-endpoint dns-zone-group create -g $RG --endpoint-name pe1 -n zg1 --private-dns-zone $ZONE --zone-name blob

t: Ask once more: now it's 10.0.2.x.
Ek dafa phir poochein: ab 10.0.2.x.
steps.cli: az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "$ASK" --query "value[0].message" -o tsv

t: Turn off public access and try from Cloud Shell: it must fail.
Public access band karein aur Cloud Shell se koshish karein: fail hona chahiye.
steps.cli:
az storage account update -n $SA -g $RG --public-network-access Disabled
KEY=$(az storage account keys list -n $SA -g $RG --query "[0].value" -o tsv)
az storage container list --account-name $SA --account-key $KEY

remember: The endpoint gives a private IP. The DNS zone makes the name use it.
Endpoint private IP deta hai. DNS zone naam ko us par le jata hai.
Each sub-service (blob, file, queue…) needs its own private endpoint.
Har sub-service (blob, file, queue…) ka apna private endpoint chahiye.

t: Load balancer and health probe
Load balancer aur health probe
goal: Balance two web servers, then stop one and see the probe react.
Do web servers balance karein, phir ek band kar ke probe ka asar dekhein.
skills: Configure an internal or public load balancer
Troubleshoot load balancing
Configure public IP addresses
Deploy virtual machines to availability zones and availability sets

t: Create the network and an NSG that allows port 80, and a file that installs nginx.
Network aur port 80 allow karne wala NSG banayen, aur nginx lagane wali file.
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab13
SIZE=Standard_B2ats_v2
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az network nsg create -g $RG -n nsg1
az network nsg rule create -g $RG --nsg-name nsg1 -n AllowHttp --priority 200 --direction Inbound --access Allow --protocol Tcp --destination-port-ranges 80 --source-address-prefixes Internet
az network vnet create -g $RG -n vnet1 --address-prefix 10.0.0.0/16 --subnet-name web --subnet-prefix 10.0.1.0/24
cat > init.yml <<'EOF'
#cloud-config
packages: [nginx]
runcmd:
  - hostname > /var/www/html/index.html
EOF

t: Create two VMs in different availability zones.
Alag availability zones mein do VMs banayen.
steps.cli: for i in 1 2; do az vm create -g $RG -n web$i --image Ubuntu2204 --size $SIZE --zone $i --vnet-name vnet1 --subnet web --nsg nsg1 --custom-data init.yml --generate-ssh-keys; done

t: Create a Standard load balancer with a probe and a rule.
Probe aur rule wala Standard load balancer banayen.
steps.cli:
az network public-ip create -g $RG -n lbpip --sku Standard --zone 1 2 3
az network lb create -g $RG -n lb1 --sku Standard --public-ip-address lbpip --frontend-ip-name fe --backend-pool-name be
az network lb probe create -g $RG --lb-name lb1 -n probe80 --protocol Http --port 80 --path /
az network lb rule create -g $RG --lb-name lb1 -n http --protocol Tcp --frontend-port 80 --backend-port 80 --frontend-ip-name fe --backend-pool-name be --probe-name probe80 --disable-outbound-snat true

t: Add both NICs to the backend pool.
Dono NICs ko backend pool mein dalein.
steps.cli: for i in 1 2; do az network nic ip-config address-pool add -g $RG --address-pool be --ip-config-name ipconfigweb$i --nic-name web${i}VMNic --lb-name lb1; done

t: Call the frontend several times: both names answer.
Frontend ko kai dafa call karein: dono naam jawab dete hain.
steps.cli:
IP=$(az network public-ip show -g $RG -n lbpip --query ipAddress -o tsv)
for i in $(seq 8); do curl -s --max-time 5 http://$IP; done

t: Stop nginx on web1, wait 30 seconds and call again: only web2 answers.
web1 par nginx band karein, 30 second rukein aur dobara call karein: sirf web2 jawab deta hai.
steps.cli:
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n web1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "systemctl stop nginx"
sleep 30
for i in $(seq 8); do curl -s --max-time 5 http://$IP; done

t: Remove the NSG rule and call once more: nothing answers, although the probe of web2 is healthy.
NSG rule hatayen aur phir call karein: koi jawab nahi, halanke web2 ka probe healthy hai.
steps.cli:
az network nsg rule delete -g $RG --nsg-name nsg1 -n AllowHttp
sleep 30
curl -s --max-time 5 http://$IP || echo "no answer"

remember: The probe passes through AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound. Client traffic needs its own rule.
Probe AllowAzureLoadBalancerInBound se guzarta hai. Client traffic ko apna rule chahiye.
A failed probe stops new connections to that VM only.
Fail probe sirf us VM ke naye connections rokta hai.

t: Alert, processing rule and VM backup
Alert, processing rule aur VM backup
goal: Get an email from a CPU alert, silence it, and back up the VM.
CPU alert se email lein, usay khamosh karein, aur VM ka backup lein.
skills: Set up alert rules, action groups, and alert processing rules in Azure Monitor
Interpret metrics in Azure Monitor
Create a Recovery Services vault
Create and configure a backup policy
Perform backup and restore operations by using Azure Backup

t: Create the VM in one group and the vault in another (the vault can't always be deleted at once).
VM ek group mein aur vault doosre mein banayen (vault hamesha foran delete nahi hota).
steps.cli:
RG=az104-lab14
VRG=az104-lab14-vault
SIZE=Standard_B2ats_v2
az group create -n $RG -l westeurope
az group create -n $VRG -l westeurope
az vm create -g $RG -n vm1 --image Ubuntu2204 --size $SIZE --generate-ssh-keys --nsg-rule NONE
az backup vault create -g $VRG -n rsv1 -l westeurope
az backup vault backup-properties set -g $VRG -n rsv1 --backup-storage-redundancy LocallyRedundant

t: Create an action group. Put your own email address in the first line.
Action group banayen. Pehli line mein apna email address likhein.
steps.cli:
EMAIL=you@example.com
az monitor action-group create -g $RG -n ag1 --action email me $EMAIL
AG=$(az monitor action-group show -g $RG -n ag1 --query id -o tsv)

t: Create a CPU alert, then load the CPU for five minutes. You get an email when it fires.
CPU alert banayen, phir paanch minute CPU par load dalein. Fire hone par email aata hai.
steps.cli:
VM_ID=$(az vm show -g $RG -n vm1 --query id -o tsv)
az monitor metrics alert create -g $RG -n cpu70 --scopes $VM_ID --condition "avg Percentage CPU > 70" --window-size 5m --evaluation-frequency 1m --action $AG
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "timeout 360 md5sum /dev/zero & timeout 360 md5sum /dev/zero; true"

t: In the portal: Monitor → Alerts. Open the alert, set the user response to Acknowledged, and see VM → Metrics → Percentage CPU.
Portal mein: Monitor → Alerts. Alert kholein, user response Acknowledged karein, aur VM → Metrics → Percentage CPU dekhein.
Silence the notifications with an alert processing rule. Load the CPU again: the alert fires, but no email comes.
Alert processing rule se notifications rokein. CPU par dobara load dalein: alert fire hota hai, email nahi aata.
steps.cli:
az monitor alert-processing-rule create -g $RG -n quiet --rule-type RemoveAllActionGroups --scopes $VM_ID
az vm run-command invoke -g $RG -n vm1 --command-id RunShellScript --scripts "timeout 360 md5sum /dev/zero & timeout 360 md5sum /dev/zero; true"

t: Protect the VM and start a backup. The first one is full and takes a while.
VM protect karein aur backup shuru karein. Pehla full hota hai aur waqt leta hai.
steps.cli:
az backup protection enable-for-vm -g $VRG -v rsv1 --vm $VM_ID --policy-name DefaultPolicy
az backup protection backup-now -g $VRG -v rsv1 -c vm1 -i vm1 --backup-management-type AzureIaasVM --retain-until $(date -d "+7 days" +%d-%m-%Y)
az backup job list -g $VRG -v rsv1 -o table

t: In the portal: vault → Backup items → Azure Virtual Machine → vm1. Look at File Recovery and Restore VM, and at Backup policies (don't restore).
Portal mein: vault → Backup items → Azure Virtual Machine → vm1. File Recovery, Restore VM aur Backup policies dekhein (restore na karein).

remember: A processing rule stops the notification, not the alert.
Processing rule notification rokta hai, alert nahi.
Deleted backup data stays soft-deleted for 14 days (free). If the vault can't be deleted yet, try again after that.
Delete hua backup data 14 din soft-deleted rehta hai (free). Vault abhi delete na ho to us ke baad koshish karein.
cleanup:
az backup protection disable -g $VRG -v rsv1 -c vm1 -i vm1 --backup-management-type AzureIaasVM --delete-backup-data true --yes
az group delete -n $RG --yes --no-wait
az backup vault delete -g $VRG -n rsv1 --yes
az group delete -n $VRG --yes --no-wait
